author: maria
purpose: What KIND of problem a claim's assessment found -- the axis that transfers across fields. `methods` records what was done to check; `our_assessment.status` records the verdict; `patterns` records the shape of the defect, so that 'every place this corpus found pseudo-replication', or 'every headline number that belongs to its instrument', is one query regardless of discipline. A pattern may sit on an ACCEPTED claim: a defect that did not change the conclusion is still a defect, and the cases where the check came back clean are what calibrate how often it matters.

anchors.makin2019: Makin TR & Orban de Xivry J-J (2019) Ten common statistical mistakes to watch out for when writing or reviewing a manuscript. eLife 8:e48175, doi:10.7554/eLife.48175. Numbered 1-10 in the paper's order (headings verified from PMC6785265 on 2026-10-16).
anchors.validity: Shadish, Cook & Campbell (2002) Experimental and Quasi-Experimental Designs for Generalized Causal Inference: statistical-conclusion, internal, construct, external validity. 'reporting' is ours: defects in what is written rather than in what was inferred.

rules: A slug enters only with at least one real instance in the corpus. No slots for patterns nobody has found.
Assign from the assessment you actually made. If the 'why' text does not describe the defect, do not tag it.
Several patterns per claim are fine; the first is the one that carries the verdict.
Before coining a new slug, run `kb.py vocab patterns` and read the definitions below.

maps_to: makin2019:3 Inflating the units of analysis
units-of-analysis-inflated.definition: Inference treats observations as independent when the predictor, the treatment or the outcome-generating process varies at a coarser level (pseudo-replication; clustered units analysed as independent).
units-of-analysis-inflated.check: Recompute at the level where the predictor varies, or cluster-bootstrap over that level; report the ICC.

nonsignificance-read-as-absence.definition: A non-significant test is reported as 'no effect', 'flat', 'no difference' or 'no interaction' without the interval or the smallest effect the design could detect.
nonsignificance-read-as-absence.check: Print the CI and the minimum detectable effect at the design's n.

maps_to: makin2019:2 Interpreting comparisons between two effects without directly comparing them
difference-in-significance-not-tested.definition: Two effects are said to differ because one is significant and the other is not, without a direct test of the difference.
difference-in-significance-not-tested.check: Test the difference (interaction or contrast) directly.

small-sample-overreach.definition: A rate, correlation or ranking is stated as general from a handful of units whose interval spans the substantive range.
small-sample-overreach.check: Exact or bootstrap interval at the true n; leave-one-out influence.

circular-analysis.definition: Units are selected, split or excluded using the outcome (or a function of it) and the same data are then used to estimate the effect, so the selection manufactures the result.
circular-analysis.check: Run the full pipeline, selection rule included, on a null world; the result should vanish.

analytic-flexibility.definition: A result depends on an analytic or processing choice that was made by inspection, changed during the project, or not disclosed, among several defensible alternatives.
analytic-flexibility.check: Rerun across the defensible alternatives; recover the undisclosed choice from code history.

null-model-misspecified.definition: The comparison distribution, baseline or permutation scheme does not represent the absence of the hypothesised effect, so departures from it are not evidence for the effect.
null-model-misspecified.check: Build the null so that it differs from the alternative ONLY in the hypothesised mechanism; calibrate it on synthetic data with the effect absent.

estimator-biased-or-insensitive.definition: The estimator is biased in the design's regime, or returns nearly the same value whatever the true quantity, so its output cannot carry the claim made from it.
estimator-biased-or-insensitive.check: Known-answer simulation over a grid of true values; plot estimate against truth.

standardiser-misdefines-effect-size.definition: A standardised effect size is divided by a spread that is not the outcome's spread across units (e.g. SD of seed means, standardised dummy predictors), so its magnitude measures precision or coding rather than effect.
standardiser-misdefines-effect-size.check: Recompute with the per-unit outcome SD and say which denominator the field means.

ratio-of-small-or-noisy-quantities.definition: A headline is a ratio (relative change, fold-change, share-of-a-difference) whose numerator or denominator is near zero or carries a standard error comparable to itself.
ratio-of-small-or-noisy-quantities.check: Report absolute differences with intervals; propagate the uncertainty into the ratio.

scale-dependent-conclusion.definition: A conclusion about interaction, additivity, homogeneity or 'no difference in effect' holds on the chosen scale and reverses or vanishes under a monotone transformation (removable interaction; additive vs multiplicative models).
scale-dependent-conclusion.check: Repeat on the scale the paper itself uses to interpret the result (log-ratio, logit, raw); state which scale the claim is about.

centre-hides-distribution.definition: A mean, median or pooled rate is reported as if it described individuals, while the distribution is a mixture, heavy-tailed, or changes shape -- the content is in the spread or the clusters.
centre-hides-distribution.check: Plot the distribution; report the share at salient values and the quantiles; test for a mixture.

mixing-incommensurable-units.definition: Quantities measured on different scales, funnels or denominators are pooled or compared as if commensurable, and the mixing produces the pattern.
mixing-incommensurable-units.check: Stratify by unit or scale; compare within strata before pooling.

maps_to: makin2019:1 Absence of an adequate control condition/group
missing-adequate-control.definition: The design lacks the condition that differs from the treatment only in the ingredient credited with the effect (matched scaffold without the content; the target absent).
missing-adequate-control.check: Name the counterfactual condition; if absent, the claim is about the package, not the ingredient.

post-treatment-conditioning.definition: Analysis adjusts for, differences against, or selects on a variable that is itself affected by the treatment or the outcome (post-treatment baselines, outcome-dependent exclusion, survivorship).
post-treatment-conditioning.check: Show the conditioning variable does not differ by arm; otherwise use a pre-treatment or separately randomised measure.

mirrored-design-common-bias.definition: In a valence-mirrored design (happy/unhappy, gain/loss, help/harm) one arm is reverse-coded before comparison, so any common directional preference appears as a valence asymmetry.
mirrored-design-common-bias.check: A separately randomised neutral arm; or show two worlds (common bias vs true asymmetry) give different cell means under the design.

correlation-read-as-causation.definition: An observational association (or an untested recommendation derived from one) is presented as the effect of the practice or property.
correlation-read-as-causation.check: Name the confounder (often a 'care' or 'disposition' proxy) and test it with a second marker of the same disposition.

instrument-relative-headline-number.definition: A headline number is fixed by the measurement procedure -- elicitation format, estimator, model order, factor-retention rule, block order -- and is cited as a property of the world.
instrument-relative-headline-number.check: Recompute under a second defensible instrument from the same data; report the spread, cite only what survives.

ceiling-or-floor-artifact.definition: A bounded measurement scale compresses or distorts a mean, a variance or a slope near its limits, and the distortion is read as substantive.
ceiling-or-floor-artifact.check: Simulate the bounded scale with the effect absent; compare the artifact's size to the reported effect.

mechanism-asserted-not-measured.definition: An explanatory mechanism is offered without measuring the quantity it names or specifying an alternative it could lose to; or the paper's own data run against it.
mechanism-asserted-not-measured.check: Find the quantity the mechanism predicts and check its direction in the paper's own tables.

target-not-identified-by-design.definition: The quantity reported is not identified by the design that produced the data: any value is compatible with the observations given an assumption the authors did not make explicit.
target-not-identified-by-design.check: Write 'design that produced it' and 'what that design identifies' (CONTRIBUTING 2b) before auditing the estimator.

population-bound-effect.definition: The effect holds in the tested population or regime (one model generation, quantisation, institution, practitioner group) and is cited as general.
population-bound-effect.check: Name the regime in every citation; find an out-of-regime replication.

denominator-unstated-or-shifted.definition: A rate is reported without the set it is over, or the denominator changes between stages, versions or comparisons without being said.
denominator-unstated-or-shifted.check: Reconstruct the funnel; find integer counts consistent with the printed rate; report every rung.

text-contradicts-own-materials.definition: A statement in the paper is contradicted by its own code, data, appendix, logs or materials.
text-contradicts-own-materials.check: Read the code and the materials against the text, line by line, for the claims that carry the conclusion.

implementation-diverges-from-definition.definition: The code computes a quantity different from the one the paper defines or names, and the published numbers carry the difference -- not a misdescription of a correct computation (that is text-contradicts-own-materials) but a different computation. Instances 2026-10-16: a need prior applied in reversed point order; a complexity counting formula nodes where the text counts atoms (imel2026-modal-typology-efficiency); a paired sign statistic reported as Cliff's delta (wu2026-chunking-rag-code-completion).
implementation-diverges-from-definition.check: Recompute one published number from the raw inputs with the paper's OWN definition. If it does not reproduce, search the space of plausible alternative definitions (orderings, counts, paired vs unpaired) until one reproduces exactly -- a unique exact match identifies what was actually computed.

paired-design-analysed-as-independent.definition: A contrast measured on the same units (same questions, same subjects, same tasks) is given the independent-samples variance. Tests become conservative, and any quantity obtained by subtracting sampling variance from observed dispersion (tau^2 in random effects, n* = sigma^2/tau^2, reliability corrections) is biased toward zero dispersion -- small heterogeneity is reported as none. Mirror image of units-of-analysis-inflated. Instances 2026-10-17: my own saturation size n* (maria2026-rag-specification-dispersion#c2, 1,134 -> 220-435 paired); wu2026 configurations (tau^2 <= 0 under the independent formula).
paired-design-analysed-as-independent.check: Compute the paired variance from per-unit outputs; if they are not released, bound it: per-item Var(d) lies in [|delta|(1-|delta|), p0(1-p0)+p1(1-p1)] for binary outcomes (upper end assumes non-negative correlation), and calibrate with a paired ratio measured on comparable data. Known-answer simulation with a shared latent per unit.
